title: General Biology
description: A beginning course in Biology stressing processes common to living organisms.
notes: Not applicable to Biological Sciences majors; see

title: General Biology Laboratory
description: A laboratory course in Biology stressing processes common to living organisms.
notes: Not applicable to Biological Sciences majors; see

title: World of Animals
description: Animal adaptation and diversity and their relationship to the development of evolutionary theory. Not applicable to Biological Sciences majors.
notes: Not open to students with credit in

title: World of Animals Laboratory
description: Laboratory course on evolution and diversity of animals involving field trips and laboratory investigations. Not applicable to Biological Sciences majors.
notes: Not open to students with credit in

title: Principles of Cell and Molecular Biology
description: Principles of biology applying to all organisms, including basic biochemistry, cell structure, membrane transport, energy metabolism, cell division, classical and molecular genetics, gene expression, development, and recombinant DNA.

title: Principles of Cell and Molecular Biology Laboratory
description: Laboratory experiences designed to demonstrate and reinforce concepts presented in lecture through active scientific investigation and experiences in observing, identifying, describing, and explaining evolution of cellular processes, and in applying laboratory methods and procedures relevant to molecular biology.

title: Principles of Organismal Biology
description: Principles of biology applying to all organisms, including systematics and diversity of bacteria, protista, fungi, plants and animals, and concepts of physiology, reproduction, development and differentiation, ecology and the causes of endangerment of a species.

title: Principles of Organismal Biology Laboratory
description: Laboratory experiences demonstrate and reinforce concepts and descriptive information presented in lecture through active scientific investigation and experience in observing, identifying, and classifying life, in analyzing the structural features of life, and in evaluating their adaptive significance.

title: Fundamentals of Microbiology
description: Microorganisms of the environment, including disease-producing organisms, their actions and reactions. For nursing, nutrition, and kinesiology (prephysical therapy) majors.
notes: Not applicable to biological sciences majors; see

title: Fundamentals of Microbiology Laboratory
description: Fundamentals of microbiology, including study of bacteria, fungi, protozoa, and algae of environment, including disease-producing organisms, their actions and reactions.

title: Human Anatomy
description: Gross and microscopic anatomy of organ system of human body.

title: Biostatistics
description: Methods and experience in defining and solving quantitative problems in biology, including design of experiments, and parametric and nonparametric statistical techniques.

title: Colloquium in Biomedical Sciences
description: Current biomedical research projects ranging from cell biology to behavioral research. Research paper required.

title: Advanced Degree Programs in the Sciences: Application Strategies
description: Instruction in preparing competitive applications to sciences’ M.S. and Ph.D. degree programs to include development of the required personal statement. Introduction to sources of financial support, such as national fellowship programs, and development of interview skills and materials.

title: Careers in Biological Sciences
description: Career opportunities in biological sciences. Specialists in major biological areas will present information about their fields and how best to prepare for careers.

title: Preprofessional Topics: Topics in Medicine
description: Designed to expose the preprofessional student to the profession of his/her choice through speakers and selected readings. Emphasis on alternatives and meeting stresses as a preprofessional student.

title: Preprofessional Topics: Topics in Dentistry
description: Designed to expose the preprofessional student to the profession of his/her choice through speakers and selected readings. Emphasis on alternatives and meeting stresses as a preprofessional student.

title: Preprofessional Topics: Topics in Veterinary Medicine
description: Designed to expose the preprofessional student to the profession of his/her choice through speakers and selected readings. Emphasis on alternatives and meeting stresses as a preprofessional student.

title: Human Anatomy Internship
description: Interns will master the material from human anatomy, develop and teach study skills, and apply skill set for administering a laboratory course in human anatomy.

title: Human Physiology
description: Human function viewed from cellular through organ system levels of organization.
notes: Intended primarily for prenursing students. Not applicable to biological sciences majors. Not open to students with credit in

title: Biostatistics Laboratory
description: Special laboratory course designed for biology majors with credit in a statistics course other than

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.
notes: See

title: Special Study
description: Individual research experience and interaction with researchers at an introductory level. Projects involve approximately 45 hours of laboratory or fieldwork per unit and a research report. Hours are flexible and arranged between the student and the researcher.

title: Biology of Sex
description: Reproductive adaptations in humans, and comparatively in other species. Topics include sex differences, mate choice and mating behavior, fertility regulation, fertilization and embryonic development, sex ratios, parental investment, effects of aging, and life history strategies.
notes: Not applicable to biological sciences majors.

title: Ecology and Human Impacts on the Environment
description: Ecological characteristics of natural ecosystems and basic effects of human society upon those systems, emphasizing resource management, food production, global environmental problems, and future directions.
notes: Not applicable to biological sciences majors.

title: World of Dinosaurs
description: Current theories and controversies surrounding the evolution and extinction of dinosaurs for non-science majors. Not applicable to biological sciences majors.

title: Life in the Sea
description: Overview of complexity of marine life. Diverse interactions of organisms in the intertidal zone, over the continental shelves and in the open oceans. Current controversies concerning the marine biosphere.
notes: Not applicable to biological sciences majors.

title: Conservation of Wildlife
description: Global ecosystems and their dynamics, with emphasis on sustainable human use and preservation of biodiversity.
notes: Not applicable to biological sciences majors. Not open to students with credit in Biology 540.

title: The Human Body
description: Survey of human body with emphasis on intricacy of design and integration of various organ systems.
notes: Not open to nursing or exercise and nutritional sciences majors, or to students with credit in any college-level human physiology or anatomy course. Not applicable to biological sciences majors.

title: Principles of Human Physiology
description: Systems of the human body, their interrelationships and control systems which regulate them.
notes: Not open to students with credit in a college course in human physiology. Not applicable to biological sciences majors.

title: Preventive Dentistry Program
description: Participation in clinic, dental observation, marketing activities and two field trips.
notes: Not applicable to biological sciences majors.

title: Preventive Dentistry Leaders
description: Supervision of one component of Preventive Dentistry Program.
notes: Not applicable to biological sciences majors.

title: General Microbiology
description: Actions and reactions of microorganisms in response to their environment, both natural and as changed by other organisms, including man. Also includes an introduction to pathogens.

title: Genetics
description: “Faulty” genes, genetic variation, human disorders. Big data, molecular, and transmission genetics.

title: Evolution
description: Principles of population genetics and evolutionary biology.

title: Ecology and the Environment
description: Fundamental concepts in population, community, and ecosystem ecology.

title: Experimental Ecology
description: Methods of research in ecology; approaches to analysis of populations, communities, and ecosystems.

title: Cell Biology
description: Fundamental processes of cell biology with an emphasis on cellular and molecular mechanisms common to eukaryotic organisms.
notes: Open only to Biology and Microbiology majors, Biology minors, and Chemistry majors with Emphasis in Biochemistry.

title: Cell Biology Laboratory
description: Basic laboratory approaches in cell biology to include operation of lab instrumentation, microscopy, and cell manipulation.

title: Human Physiology Laboratory
description: Human physiology and rationale of current week’s laboratory and experimental outcomes of previous week’s laboratory.
notes: Not open to students with credit in

title: Science Concept Development and Integration
description: Development and integration of biological science content knowledge, introduction to learning theory, and transformation of knowledge. Designed for students preparing for the single subject teaching credential in life sciences.

title: Plant Biology
description: Cell biology and structure, photosynthesis, respiration, secondary metabolism, physiology of water relations and transport, growth and development, evolution of major groups, plant ecology of Southern California and topics related to agriculture. Same course as lecture portion of

title: Zoology
description: Biology and ecology of animals to include diversity and evolution, morphological and behavioral adaptations to environments, physiological mechanisms, and relationships to world ecosystems.

title: Functional Genomics Laboratory
description: Practical research experience in cell and molecular biology using an applicable model system(s). Analysis of gene expression, gene inhibition approaches, image data analysis, microscopy techniques, and/or molecular genetic techniques.

title: Learning Assistant Professional Development for the Biological Sciences
description: Preparation of undergraduate learning assistants to support biology student learning in the Ecological and Evolutionary Sciences. Covers core topics in teaching and learning including learning cognition, effective feedback, group work, classroom equity and diversity, and core biology content areas.
notes: Students must contact the department for approval to enroll.

title: Clinical Hematology
description: Theoretical and practical background for study of normal and pathological blood cells to include laboratory techniques. Course meets State of California requirements as a hematology course for students entering training programs in clinical laboratory sciences.

title: Principles of Immunology
description: Basic areas of immunology to include inflammation, generation of immune response, antibody production, lymphocyte development and function, hypersensitivities and AIDS, major histocompatibility complex and cytokines. Designed to give a basic background in the immune system.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study, internship, other supervised laboratory or field project or experience. Credit involves 50 hour activity per unit per semester. Written or oral presentation of results required.
notes: Students must contact the instructort for approval to enroll in this course. Limit of six units of any combination of 495 and 497 applicable to a bachelor’s degree. Not open to students with six units of credit in BIOL 499.

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.
notes: See

title: Undergraduate Research
description: Independent research project supervised by faculty. Data analysis and written or oral presentation of results.
notes: Students must contact the instructor for approval to enroll in this course. Limit of six units of any combination of 495 and 497 applicable to a bachelor’s degree.

title: Classics of Biology
description: Review and discussion of classic literature in the biological and environmental sciences that has shaped modern biological thought.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Advanced Evolution
description: Evolutionary biology including genetics of populations, speciation, systematic biology, adaptation, role of development in evolution, evolution of behavior, and comparative biology. Evolutionary biology as the central organizing principle of biology.
notes: See Class Schedule for specific content. Limit of nine units of any combination of 296, 496, 596 courses applicable to a bachelor’s degree. Credit for 596 and 696 applicable to a master’s degree with approval of the graduate adviser.

title: Molecular Evolution
description: Molecular evolution including concepts of homology and convergence, the nearly neutral theory of evolution, evolution of new protein function, detecting selection, multi-gene family evolution and evolutionary genomics.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Evolution and Ecology of Marine Mammals
description: Biology of marine mammals including pinniped, cetacean and sirenian evolution, diet and foraging strategies, social organization, reproductive strategies, echolocation, diving physiology, and conservation.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Biology of the Algae
description: Evolution, life histories, morphology, physiology, and ecology of micro and macro algae, with attention to both marine and freshwater taxa, and of sea-grasses.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Marine Invertebrate Biology
description: Structure and function, ecology, behavior, physiology and phyletic relationships of marine invertebrate animals.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Marine Larval Ecology Research Part 1
description: Biology of marine invertebrate larvae. Biodiversity, evolution of complex life cycles, larval culture techniques, physiological and ecological consequences of environmental variability during larval development. Designing and peer reviewing original research proposals related to larval ecology.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Marine Larval Ecology Research Part 2
description: Research experience investigating marine invertebrate larval ecology.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Marine Ecology
description: Ecological concepts as applied to pelagic and benthic marine organisms and their environment. Field and laboratory experience in oceanographic techniques, particularly the coastal environment. Field and laboratory experience in oceanographic techniques, particularly the coastal environment.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Biology of Fishes
description: Ecology, anatomy, physiology, evolution, taxonomy, environmental constraints, habitats, feeding, behavior, growth, reproduction, biotic interactions, population dynamics, and assemblage structure. Fisheries biology concepts to include stock-recruitment models, density dependence and population regulation, management of fisheries, and conservation.
notes: Not open to students with credit in Biology 520 and 541.

title: Herpetology
description: Evolution, systematics, distribution, and ecology of amphibians and reptiles of the world.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Ornithology
description: Study and identification of birds, especially those of the Pacific Coast and the San Diego region.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Mammalogy
description: Evolution, systematics, distribution and ecology of mammals of the world.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Terrestrial Arthropod Biology
description: Behavior, ecology, evolution, function, relationships, and structure of major groups of terrestrial arthropods, including arachnids, insects, and myriapods. Identification and natural history of southern California diversity.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Animal Behavior
description: Biological bases of animal behavior with emphasis on ethological approach, including evolution and adaptive significance of behavior.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Microbial Ecology
description: Roles of microorganisms in soil, aquatic and marine ecosystems, microbial adaptations to the environment, and interactions within microbial communities and between microbes and multicellular organisms. Laboratory techniques to isolate and study microbes.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Plant Systematics
description: Plant description, identification, classification, and nomenclature with emphasis on evolutionary patterns, interdisciplinary data acquisition, and phylogenetic analysis.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Taxonomy of California Plants
description: Fundamentals of plant taxonomy with emphasis on identification of plants native and naturalized to California. Plant collecting techniques. Field trips are required.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Plant Ecology
description: Plant adaptation and response to living and non-living environment including aspects of plant evolution, demography, ecophysiology community and ecosystem dynamics and soil-plant relationships. Terrestrial systems emphasized.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Conservation Ecology
description: Human impacts on ecosystems, the resultant endangerment and extinction of plant and animal species, and strategies for the protection and recovery of threatened forms.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Ecological Signaling in the Environment
description: Ecological consequences of species interactions mediated by signals in terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems. Evaluating primary literature and conveying science to a broad audience.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Terrestrial Ecosystems and Climate Change
description: Controls on fluxes and stocks of nutrients within terrestrial ecosystems, ecosystem responses, feedbacks to climate change. Climate systems, water transport, production and decomposition, nutrient cycling, stable isotopes, spatial and temporal integration.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Microbial Genetics and Physiology
description: Physiology of microbial growth, bacterial structure and function, genetics of bacteriophages and bacteria.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Molecular Virology
description: Molecular aspects of structure, genetics, and replication of viruses, virus-host interactions, pathogenesis of virus infections, diagnostic virology, and antiviral vaccines and drugs; emphasis on human pathogens.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Scanning Electron Microscopy Laboratory
description: Biological specimen preparation and operation of scanning electron microscope.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Transmission Electron Microscopy Laboratory
description: Biological sample preparation and operation of transmission electron microscope.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Animal Physiology
description: Physiology of vertebrate and invertebrate animals with emphasis on diversity of solutions to physiological problems and on functional integration of organ systems.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Ecological Metagenomics
description: Next generation DNA sequencing technology with emphasis on ecological applications in microbial communities. Metagenomic analysis of taxonomic identification, physiological function, and the ecological role of the microbial community in the broader ecosystem.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Principles of Cancer Biology
description: Fundamental concepts of cancer biology, including modern experimental techniques in cancer research. Exploration of primary research articles and cutting-edge discoveries in the field of cancer biology.
notes: It is recommended that students take CHEM 365 before this course, but it is not required.

title: Genome Editing
description: Fundamental concepts in DNA manipulation and gene expression, including training in CRISPR gene editing technology.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Advanced Biochemistry, Cellular, and Molecular Biology
description: Advanced concepts of cellular biology, molecular biology, and biochemistry.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Biochemistry, Cellular, and Molecular Biology Laboratory II
description: Intermediate laboratory approaches to biochemistry, cellular biology, and molecular biology at a level appropriate for both advanced undergraduate and graduate students.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Bioinformatics
description: Bioinformatics analysis methods and programming skills. Practical bioinformatic software for sequence analysis, bioinformatic algorithms and programming fundamentals.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Neurobiology
description: Structure and function of the nervous system to include cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying neuronal excitability and synaptic function, nervous system development, cellular and systems analysis of sensory, motor and higher brain functions. Emphasis on experimental approaches.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Molecular Basis of Heart Disease
description: Current literature on the molecular basis of disordered physiology leading to heart disease.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Developmental Biology
description: Fundamental processes of development from fertilized egg to organism. Emphasis on cellular and molecular mechanisms common to development of metazoan organisms.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Environmental Systems Modeling: Principles and Application
description: Development and application of numerical models for the analysis of environmental and ecological systems and problems, with a focus on terrestrial ecosystems in the context of global environmental change.

title: Research Methods in Biology
description: An intensive semester-long lecture, field, and laboratory course illustrating research methods from molecular-to-ecosystem levels of biological organization. Students learn and practice these research methods using plant/animal/microbial/viral model systems. Includes experimental design, data analyses, and results dissemination (oral and written).

title: Medical Microbiology
description: Major bacterial and viral pathogens; molecular mechanisms of pathogenesis, microbial toxins and antimicrobial agents; immune response to microbial infections; biochemical and molecular diagnostics.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Cellular and Molecular Immunology
description: Cellular and molecular aspects of the immune response. Genetics of immunoglobulins, major histocompatibility complex, lymphocyte development and their manifestations on immune responsiveness, lymphokines immunopathologies including AIDS, and contemporary immunological techniques.
notes: Not open to students with credit in

title: Stem Cell and Regenerative Biology
description: Stem cell basics, cloning, tissue engineering, research on animal models of regeneration, political and ethical issues surrounding stem cell debate.
notes: Writing Requirement for Undergraduates: Completion of the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement or the eligibility to enroll in an upper division writing course is a prerequisite for all upper division biology courses numbered 450 and above.

title: Physiology of Human Systems
description: Human physiology presented at both cellular and organ system levels; neurophysiology, muscle physiology, cardiovascular physiology and respiration, kidney function, hormone function and reproduction.
notes: For students majoring in a natural science or pre-professional studies.

title: Special Topics in Biology
description: Advanced selected topics in modern biology.
notes: See

title: Undergraduate Thesis
description: Experience in designing and carrying out independent research in a laboratory or field setting plus a written record of experimental design and results in the form of a research thesis to be defended before a committee.
notes: Students must contact the instructor for approval to enroll in this course. BIOL 597 is not applicable to a graduate degree.

title: Seminar
description: An intensive study in advanced biology.
notes: See

title: Seminar in Biology
description: An intensive study in advanced biological concepts involving discussion of topical scientific literature.

title: Univariate Statistical Methods in Biology
description: Application of univariate statistical techniques in biological sciences.

title: Biological Data
description: Concepts and applications of advanced statistical techniques in the biological sciences to include multivariate statistics, analysis of discrete data, spatial statistics, time series analysis, and Monte Carlo methods (e.g. bootstrapping and randomization tests).

title: Population Genetics
description: Theoretical and applied population genetics to include genetic diversity in natural populations, random drift, mutation, gene flow, natural selection, nucleotide variation, and quantitative genetics. Emphasis on data analysis and interpretation.

title: Theory and Principles of Ecology I
description: Major theoretical concepts in ecology, topics of current interest, and historical context of central ideas in ecology, with emphasis on use of primary literature.
